grounding.quote: `id` fields own identities rather than reference them.

A required reference
that `model_validation` leaves unresolved, its resolution still open as
AC-007 defines for `gap`, is not refused:

constraints.statement: Identity fields own rather than reference identities. Digests, closed enums, predicates, unlisted qualifier content, uncertainty, consequence, variation content and refusal values are closed non-reference content. Every list is duplicate-free before set comparison. Missing rows, targets outside their rows, wrong local populations/sorts, unresolved external targets, cardinality violations and basis-relation mismatches refuse model validation, subject to the explicit open-resolution gap distinction. grounding.quote:
| `claim-admission` | exact `RelationClaim` | exact claim and claim-judgment refs; source frontier equals the claim frontier; occurrence ref follows `scope_class` |
| `occurrence-admission` | exact `Occurrence` | `occurrence_scoped`; occurrence ref equals the payload ref; claim fields absent |
| `effect-disposition` | exact `EffectDisposition` | `occurrence_scoped`; occurrence ref equals the invocation's occurrence; claim fields absent |
| `external-fact-admission` | exact non-event `ProfileRecordRef` | `subject_scoped` or `authority_scoped`; occurrence and claim fields absent |

constraints.statement: event_kind_ref resolves exactly one of the four closed exact identities; short labels are aliases for those identities. claim-admission requires an exact RelationClaim payload, exact claim/judgment references, source frontier identical to the claim frontier and occurrence binding according to scope_class. occurrence-admission requires an Occurrence payload, occurrence_scoped scope, occurrence_ref equal to payload_ref and absent claim fields. effect-disposition requires an EffectDisposition payload, occurrence_scoped scope, occurrence_ref equal to the invocation's occurrence and absent claim fields. external-fact-admission requires a non-event ProfileRecordRef payload, subject_scoped or authority_scoped scope and absent occurrence/claim fields. grounding.quote:
Every relation, and every `RelationClaim.value.relation_qualifiers`, has
exactly those nine fields and satisfies the contract its exact relation
kind selects.

constraints.statement: Every relation and RelationClaim.relation_qualifiers has exactly cardinality, authority_ref, evidence_refs, provenance_refs, invalidation_ref, inverse_kind_ref_or_none, preservation, loss and refusal; inherited fields cannot be omitted. Closed enums: cardinality={exactly_one,zero_or_one,zero_or_more,one_or_more}; preservation={identity_preserved,meaning_preserved,not_applicable}; loss={none,declared_loss}; refusal={refuse_missing,refuse_duplicate,refuse_wrong_type,refuse_invalid_basis,refuse_out_of_scope,not_applicable}. Every core relation fixes preservation=meaning_preserved, loss=none, inverse_kind_ref_or_none=none and refusal to one of the five refuse_* values; not_applicable is unavailable. Authority, evidence, provenance and invalidation references are exact instance coordinates. The five identity-bearing fields resolve through the finite table; the four enums use only their closed domains. Missing/extra fields, duplicate refs, unknown enums, kind/cardinality mismatches, incompatible preservation, declared loss, non-null inverse, unavailable refusal, unresolved qualifier identities or qualifier-basis mismatch refuse structural admission. Materialisation copies the accepted qualifiers byte for byte.

exceptions: disposition_for has exactly one target for each disposition other than no_effect, and none for no_effect.
admits_claim and materializes_relation are required exactly once for claim-admission events; the event-kind table excludes claim fields on other kinds.

grounding.quote:
`Cardinality_occurrence` is this total function over the
closed core relation-kind population (P3, P5):

Every claim-admission event has exactly
one `admits_claim` and exactly one `materializes_relation`.

constraints.statement: The exact cardinality qualifier is exactly_one for application_of, applies_traversal, bound_to_subject, intends, operation_of_kind, targets_subject, authorized_by, projects_frontier, admits_claim, materializes_relation and transition_for; zero_or_one for observes_before, observes_after, invokes_effect, disposition_for, event_for and component_of_occurrence; zero_or_more for evidenced_by, frontier_contains, identity_depends_on, causally_precedes_occurrence, causally_precedes_event, supports_event and corrects_event. Singleton relations exist exactly once for their applicable subjects. Identity, causal, support, correction, component, frontier-membership and evidence populations are finite and duplicate-free. inverse_kind_ref_or_none is explicit; silence implies no inverse.

grounding.quote:
For every occurrence `o`, the value preimage and the typed relations are
exactly congruent (P3):

constraints.statement: For every occurrence o: target(application_of(o))=o.application_ref; that application's traversal_ref=o.traversal_ref and functor_kind_ref=o.functor_kind_ref; target(applies_traversal(application_of(o).target))=o.traversal_ref; target(bound_to_subject(o))=o.subject_binding_ref; target(intends(o))=o.intended_outcome_ref; targets(identity_depends_on with source o)=set(o.identity_dependency_refs); sources(causally_precedes_occurrence with target o) union sources(component_of_occurrence with target o)=set(o.lineage_refs). List uniqueness, relation-identity uniqueness and exact (kind,source,target) triple uniqueness must hold before set equality; set conversion cannot erase duplicates. Duplicate, missing, extra, reversed or mismatched edges refuse occurrence_admission; labels cannot repair a different identity preimage. lineage_refs contains only admitted occurrence-cause predecessors and aggregate component occurrences, never support, correction, timestamp, ordinal, adjacency or correlation edges.

conditions: Each constraint is evaluated only on its named record kind and within its declared scope.
constraints.statement: Every predicate returns exactly one of satisfied, falsified, indeterminate or invalid_basis. The source excludes out_of_frame because evaluation stays inside applies_to and scope, not because missing declarations are false. satisfied maps to the first, positive judgment decision; invalid_basis maps only to invalid_basis. An event's declared scope conflicting with admitting authority falsifies event_scope_compatible and yields out_of_scope, distinct from out_of_frame. Omitted results, residuals and stops cannot be converted to success. Judgment kind, not incidental prose, determines applicable stops and residuals.

grounding.quote: | Judgment kind | Unchanged subject | Decision domain | Required evidence | Stop, residual, and re-entry law |

constraints.statement: Exact closed judgment contracts: model_validation(OccurrenceModelSubject) decisions={valid,hold,refused,invalid_basis}, evidence=exact model id/digest, profile basis and typed graph populations; refusal or invalid basis, with open unresolved refs retaining gap until repair. occurrence_admission(Occurrence)={admitted,hold,refused,invalid_basis}, evidence=exact id/digest and resolved pre-existing seed inputs; missing seed retains hold+unresolved_cause and re-entry uses a new complete occurrence candidate. event_admission(FrameworkEvent)={admitted,hold,refused,invalid_basis,out_of_scope}, evidence=event id/digest, payload digest, scope authority, source frontier; unresolved scope retains hold+unresolved_scope; incompatible scope refuses. claim_admission(RelationClaim)={admitted,hold,refused,invalid_basis}, evidence=claim id/digest, endpoints, qualifiers, claimant authority, current source frontier; unresolved cause or stale frontier retains hold and re-entry uses a new claim over the current frontier. semantic_cut_admission(SemanticAdmissionCut)={admitted,hold,refused,invalid_basis}, evidence=exact seven-member cut and source/successor equality law; incomplete/inconsistent cut refuses, stale source retains hold+stale_frontier and requires reconstruction. effect_readiness(EffectSubject)={ready,stale,unauthorized,hold,invalid_basis}, evidence=pre-observation, invocation, operation, grant, territory, invalidation state; stale yields hold+stale_currentness and re-observation; unauthorized yields refusal and no dispatch. transition_evaluation(TransitionSubject)={satisfied,falsified,partial,indeterminate,refused,invalid_basis}, evidence=exact pre/post observations, intended outcome, disposition, bounded effect evidence; partial yields partial_effect; indeterminate retains hold plus declared residual; refused yields refusal. frontier_projection(Projection)={admitted,hold,gap,refused,invalid_basis}, evidence=projection/frontier ids/digests, complete members, basis, precedence law, boundary, residuals; stale retains hold+stale_frontier; unresolved lineage retains gap; re-entry uses a new projection.

grounding.quote: | Constraint kind | Subject | Deciding judgment | `falsified` mapping | `indeterminate` mapping |

constraints.statement: For each following row, mappings are ordered falsified; indeterminate. identity_dependency_acyclic, occurrence_causation_acyclic and event_causation_acyclic apply to OccurrenceModelSubject via model_validation: refused+refusal; hold+unresolved_cause. occurrence_seed_complete applies to Occurrence via occurrence_admission: refused+refusal; hold+unresolved_cause. relation_claim_admissible applies to RelationClaim via claim_admission: refused+refusal; hold+(unresolved_cause or stale_frontier). semantic_cut_complete applies to SemanticAdmissionCut via semantic_cut_admission: refused+refusal; hold+stale_frontier. pre_effect_current applies to EffectSubject via effect_readiness: stale+hold+stale_currentness; hold+stale_currentness. operation_grant_contains_effect applies to EffectSubject via effect_readiness: unauthorized+refusal; hold+unobserved_subject_state. event_scope_compatible applies to FrameworkEvent via event_admission: out_of_scope+refusal; hold+unresolved_scope. frontier_complete applies to Projection via frontier_projection: refused+refusal; hold+stale_frontier. transition_subject_complete applies to TransitionSubject via transition_evaluation: refused+refusal; indeterminate+unobserved_subject_state.

grounding.quote: | Residual kind | Subject | Required re-entry |

constraints.statement: Residual kinds fix their subject and required re-entry: unobserved_subject_state(SubjectBinding)→acquire bounded observation or retain hold; partial_effect(EffectInvocation)→acquire post-observation and explicit disposition; unresolved_cause(claim or event)→acquire authority and evidence or retain unresolved; unresolved_scope(FrameworkEvent)→declare lawful scope or refuse admission; competing_lineage(EventFrontier)→apply authorized frontier_projection judgment; stale_frontier(Projection)→construct a new exact frontier and projection; stale_currentness(EffectSubject)→re-observe and re-judge before effect; unobserved_external_mutation(SubjectBinding)→observe or retain explicit material unknown.

grounding.quote:
A judgment decision is the evaluation's result and a stop is the step's.
Where values emitted together map to different core values, as `stale`
with `hold` does, each answers its own predicate.

constraints.statement: Each refined result maps to exactly one core value for its own predicate, retaining vocabulary, residual and re-entry. Judgment decisions answer whether the first decision listed for that judgment holds for the unchanged subject on the exact basis; stops answer whether the traversal application can reach its declared result on the exact basis; effect dispositions answer whether the intended effect occurred. The stop predicate is not construction availability. Co-emitted values answer independently, so stale and hold can map differently; no value counts toward another predicate. Cause-dependent values carry cause as part of the refinement without adding a kind.
constraints.uncertainty: Imported core-result and conjunction laws are referenced, not independently reconstructed.

grounding.quote:
A refusal's cause is the one that the operation-outcome
rows `refusal(constraint)` and `refusal(basis)` of
[AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS AC-007](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#ac-007-constraint-and-refusal)
state for the conditions the refusal names:

constraints.statement: refusal(basis) names only conditions of the basis acted on, with no demonstrated violation by the subject under judgment; a violation inside an input used as basis belongs here. Pure coordinate/basis, basis-relation, qualifier-basis and cross-basis edge mismatches are mixed-basis conditions, not structural counterexamples. A qualifier recording this cause uses refuse_invalid_basis. refusal(constraint) names a demonstrated subject violation, whatever basis conditions it also names, or otherwise names no AC-007 basis condition; it follows a falsified table, structural or lawful-scope constraint. Qualifiers recording this cause use refuse_missing, refuse_duplicate, refuse_wrong_type or refuse_out_of_scope. A seed falsifying completeness, incompatible declared event scope, scope still undeclared when unresolved_scope re-entry closes, and duplicate/missing/extra/reversed/mismatched edges are subject defects. Closure without lawful scope retains unresolved_scope and re-enters with a new lawful event candidate. Any co-named basis condition is separately reported as invalid_basis; a co-emitted invalid_basis decision keeps its own predicate and does not erase a demonstrated violation. refused(basis) or refused(constraint) follows the cause of the yielded refusal. Qualifiers record, never choose, the cause. The same defect may affect a different operation that uses the record as its basis.

grounding.quote:
- `partial_effect(not_attained)`: the admitted evidence establishes that
  the intended outcome is not met and that no later completion of the
  effect can meet it.

Falsified never licenses treating the effect as absent; indeterminate
never licenses treating it as absent or as complete;

constraints.statement: partial_effect(not_attained) requires admitted evidence and bounded post-observation, read under outcome contract/comparison basis, establishing both non-attainment and impossibility of attainment by later completion. Examples include ending short, a closed outcome interval, or an irreversible outcome-defeating part; effect termination itself is not required for this cause. Every other partial_effect is undecided: missing post-observation, possible later completion, an outcome temporarily met while continuing effects may change it, or lost response without counterexample. Lost response, absent record or absent actor-context trace proves neither non-attainment nor effect termination. transition_evaluation.partial takes the corresponding not_attained/undecided cause of its partial_effect stop. Both partial and partial_effect(not_attained) map to falsified; undecided maps to indeterminate. The core value does not preserve subject-change or termination facts: the partial_effect residual and re-entry preserve both through every join. Neither value licenses absence or unproved termination; indeterminate also does not license completion. Explicit re-entry precedes any further effect, and unestablished termination requires reconciliation under ACTIVATION §5 before repetition.

grounding.quote:
The remaining judgment decisions follow the constraint rule above: the
first decision each judgment lists maps to satisfied;

constraints.statement: Stops map as follows: hold→indeterminate, because deciding evidence is not admitted; gap→invalid_basis while required reference/lineage resolution is open; refusal(constraint)→falsified; refusal(basis)→invalid_basis; invalid_basis→invalid_basis; out_of_scope→falsified only for declared scope incompatible with authority and emitted with refusal; partial_effect(not_attained)→falsified; partial_effect(undecided)→indeterminate. An undeclared scope retains hold+unresolved_scope while re-entry remains open, and closure without declaration yields refusal(constraint), not out_of_scope. Decisions: each first-listed positive decision→satisfied; out_of_scope, unauthorized and stale→falsified; hold→indeterminate; gap→invalid_basis; invalid_basis, transition falsified and transition indeterminate map to their namesake core values; refused(constraint)→falsified; refused(basis)→invalid_basis; partial causes map as specified. Missing required transition post-observation produces indeterminate+unobserved_subject_state. These mappings hold for every traversal under the signature; a traversal cannot remap them.

exceptions: A refusal naming only a basis mismatch takes the basis cause.
Open required-reference resolution is gap, whereas an evaluated no-target reference is dangling and refuses.

grounding.quote:
A structural refusal is one whose source is this profile's closed
structure rather than a row of the constraint table:

constraints.statement: Structural counterexamples include unknown/missing required value fields; missing populations, hidden records, ambiguous refs, unknown record kinds, undeclared field domains; finite-domain missing rows, outside-row targets, wrong population/sort, unresolved external target, cardinality/nested-coordinate/witness defects; unknown event kind, wrong payload sort, digest mismatch and forbidden event fields; qualifier defects, references outside the closed union or declared domain, and duplicate/missing/extra/reversed/mismatched edges. The closed structure is the predicate and the defect its counterexample, yielding refusal(constraint)/refused(constraint), not automatically invalid_basis merely because the source is structural. A qualifier retains the missing/duplicate/wrong-type/out-of-scope/invalid-basis distinction beside the core value.

grounding.quote:
Two applications of one traversal over one subject are two occurrences. A
retry or a continuation creates a fresh occurrence only when it reapplies
the traversal.

constraints.statement: Occurrence identity binds only facts available before admission. Exclude post-effect observations, effect evidence, judgments, admitted events, timestamps, admission ordinals and projection results from its seed; they may point to the occurrence after their own identities exist. The application identity pre-exists and has the same traversal/functor-kind fields; declared lineage/dependency inputs equal the exact populations of the congruence law. Mirroring relations are minted after occurrence identity and reproduce its endpoints without entering the seed. Two applications of one traversal to one subject are distinct occurrences. Retry/continuation creates a fresh occurrence only upon traversal reapplication; later controller steps, observations, waits or correlation records are not thereby occurrences. Every retained bracketed application under AC-016 has its own occurrence; an applied composite additionally has an aggregate occurrence, with component_of_occurrence links that imply no material cause. Required intermediate results, judgments, evidence, authority, provenance and stops stay explicit.
constraints.uncertainty: AC-016's full composition law is outside the supplied source.

grounding.quote:
The directed graph formed by `identity_depends_on` is finite and acyclic.
Every dependency target exists before the dependent identity is minted.

constraints.statement: identity_depends_on forms a finite DAG. Every target exists before its dependent identity is minted; no future result or event may enter its own occurrence seed.

conditions: Admission of a relation claim.

grounding.quote:
Only `j_c.decision = admitted`, `j_e.decision = admitted` and
`j_a.decision = admitted` together admit the complete semantic cut.

constraints.statement: The source-defined sequence is claim c → judgment j_c over unchanged c → candidate event e binding c,j_c,F_k → judgment j_e over unchanged e → deterministic relation r from (c,j_c,e,j_e,basis) → successor frontier → cut a=(c,j_c,e,j_e,r,F_k,F_k_plus_1) → judgment j_a over unchanged a. Only all three admitted decisions admit the complete cut. c,j_c,e,j_e,r,a,j_a have distinct identities and authority; construction does not admit, judgments do not rewrite subjects, and events inherit no candidate authority. Materialisation preserves accepted kind, endpoints, qualifiers and basis. j_c/j_e/j_a have kinds claim_admission/event_admission/semantic_cut_admission, exact subject identities c/e/a and SHA-256 of each subject's canonical bytes. Each carries full inherited context, owner, scope, basis, evaluator, authority, decision, evidence, provenance and decision-time fields. Missing cut judgment, non-admitted decision, wrong subject/digest or cross-basis judgment refuses the cut.
constraints.uncertainty: This records an authored sequence without executing or proving it.

conditions: A claim-admission cut.

grounding.quote:
The source and successor
frontiers also share `projection_basis_ref` and `precedence_law_ref`, and
the only permitted difference in frontier content is the addition of
`e.id` once.

constraints.statement: Admission-event identity binds kind, payload digest, scope, optional occurrence, exact claim, claim judgment, source frontier, owner and basis. Materialized-relation identity binds unchanged claim, claim judgment, event, event judgment and profile basis. frontier_contains(F,e) holds iff e appears once in F.member_event_refs, with neither representation containing extras or omissions. Claim-admission uses its exact event-kind URN and c.source_frontier_ref=e.source_frontier_ref=a.source_frontier_ref, by identity rather than equivalence or adjacency. All seven cut references resolve unchanged judged/materialized records. All seven subjects, three judgments and three required relations share the exact profile basis; both frontiers share projection basis and precedence law and differ only by e.id added once. The exact required edges are admits_claim(e,c), materializes_relation(e,r), frontier_contains(F_k_plus_1,e), each with inherited shape and closed qualifiers. Missing, extra, reversed, duplicate or cross-basis required edges refuse; source frontier already containing e or duplicate members refuses before set comparison. First events need no fictional predecessor. Re-admission with the same claim, claim judgment, event judgment, source frontier, basis and authority returns the existing byte-equal cut; nonidentical collisions refuse_duplicate and mint no rival facts. Pre-admission claim endpoints already exist; generated admits_claim/materializes_relation records are post-admission relations, not self-future claims.

conditions: A relation claim is admitted.

grounding.quote:
Missing,
conflicting or inconsistent members refuse the cut. This atomicity is
semantic; the profile prescribes no storage or transaction mechanism

constraints.statement: One admitted cut contains the unchanged claim, its judgment, event with scope and judgment, deterministic materialized relation, exact source frontier and unique successor. Claim, event and cut name one identical source frontier; successor equals it plus exactly the admitted event. Missing, conflicting or inconsistent members refuse. Atomicity is semantic, with no prescribed storage or transaction mechanism.

conditions: corrects_event(new, existing).

grounding.quote:
`corrects_event(new, existing)` keeps both immutable events. A correction
changes later projection through an explicit selection law; it does not
delete, rewrite or retrospectively re-identify the corrected fact

constraints.statement: Keep both immutable events. Correction changes later projection through an explicit selection law; it cannot delete, rewrite or retrospectively re-identify the corrected fact.

grounding.quote:
Cause is established only by
an admitted causal claim under competent authority and evidence.

constraints.statement: Identity, occurrence-cause and event-cause graphs remain distinct and each acyclic under its own type. Cause requires an admitted causal claim with competent authority and evidence. Timestamp, ordinal, adjacency, containment, common subject, shared actor, correlation and arrival order create no cause. Opposing differently typed edges, such as support one way and correction the other, are lawful; an untyped-union cycle is causal only if a declared causal subgraph itself cycles.

conditions: A declared precedence coordinate is used to select current truth.

grounding.quote:
The coordinate, its comparison law, its basis and its admitting
authority are explicit.

constraints.statement: Declare the coordinate, comparison law, basis and admitting authority explicitly. The coordinate orders eligible facts and gains no semantic, admission, causal or decision authority.

exceptions: Exact territory equality may be replaced only by an explicit authority-owned containment relation in an adopting Product's compatible signature.

grounding.quote:
No operation is lawful without a matching grant that names the subject
binding, the operation kind and the effect territory.

constraints.statement: Functor kind, traversal, operation, executor, actor, grant and invocation are distinct coordinates. F_P/F_D/F_H classification alone neither identifies, authorizes nor executes an operation; profile construction and occurrence admission mint no grant. Invocation.operation_ref=operation.id; operation_of_kind target=operation.operation_kind_ref; targets_subject target=operation.subject_binding_ref; authorized_by target=invocation.operation_grant_ref=grant.id. Operation, grant and occurrence subject bindings are identical; operation.kind belongs to grant.allowed_operation_kind_refs; operation.contract equals the exact OperationKind object's contract; operation, invocation and grant territories are identical absent the stated containment extension. Exact OperationKind closes both kind and contract: same labels with different contract, target sort, invalidated kind or unresolved kind reference cannot be authorized. Nominal kind equality, role labels, executor access and broad workspace access do not satisfy a grant.

grounding.quote:
`j_ready` judges the unchanged `EffectSubject` immediately before effect
dispatch under the application's declared currentness and invalidation
law.

`invokes_effect` exists if and only if a concrete invocation was
dispatched; `unauthorized` or `stale` readiness never dispatches it.

constraints.statement: The described effect sequence observes W under the stable binding, constructs the invocation/readiness subject, judges readiness immediately before dispatch, dispatches on ready, observes the resulting W and judges the transition. Stale observation or grant prevents starting: re-observe and issue a new readiness subject/judgment or stop. Unauthorized and stale never dispatch; invokes_effect exists iff a concrete invocation was dispatched. no_effect has no dispatched invocation and records no attempted domain effect. completed_effect binds one dispatched invocation, bounded post-observation and sufficient evidence. partial_effect binds one dispatched invocation, bounded post-observation/evidence, partial_effect residual and stop, and explicit re-entry before further effect; when begun effects cannot establish complete disposition, keep partial_effect explicit and require bounded post-effect observation. refused_effect binds the refused invocation attempt and refusal stop with evidence no authorized mutation began. Disposition never rewrites the immutable invocation. No lock or transaction implementation is required.

conditions: An EffectInvocation names the occurrence, so the occurrence intends an effect and the predicate is 'the intended effect occurred'.
exceptions: If no EffectInvocation names the occurrence, it intends no effect; no_effect is only a no-attempt record and no effect-result predicate is posed.

grounding.quote:
An occurrence that no `EffectInvocation` names intends no effect.
ACTIVATION §3 Effects poses no predicate for it, and its `no_effect`
records only that no domain effect was attempted: it is a record, not an
effect result (P5, P6).

constraints.statement: completed_effect→completed→satisfied requires evidence the intended effect occurred and ended. partial_effect(not_attained)→not_effected→falsified requires non-attainment impossible to repair by later completion, with the part that occurred and any unknown termination retained beside the value. partial_effect(undecided)→completion_unknown→indeterminate preserves undecidability. refused_effect→not_effected→falsified establishes no authorized mutation began. Applicable no_effect→not_effected→falsified records no dispatch, hence no effect on the subject. These mappings inform reliance/repetition without erasing partial mutation or unknown termination.

conditions: A later traversal application occurs and authority is unchanged.

grounding.quote:
A later traversal application observes the then-current
`W` under the stable binding when authority is unchanged (P3, P0).

constraints.statement: Observe then-current W under the stable binding. Descriptive artifacts cannot replace W, and a new occurrence implies no rollback.

conditions: A traversal is reapplied over an evolving external subject.

grounding.quote:
Iteration does not mutate an earlier occurrence. Each traversal
reapplication mints a fresh immutable occurrence over the evolving
subject, so the admitted occurrence and event history is append-only even
when the external subject changes repeatedly (P3, P4b).

constraints.statement: Mint a fresh immutable occurrence; never mutate an earlier occurrence. Admitted occurrence/event history remains append-only even if the external subject changes repeatedly.

grounding.quote:
For profile basis `b`, scope `s` and precedence law `p` there is one empty
frontier `F_0(b,s,p)`.

constraints.statement: For every exact profile basis b, scope s and precedence law p there is one empty F_0(b,s,p). Admitting e constructs a successor with exactly members(F_k) union {e}. Frontier identity binds basis, scope, precedence law, sorted event identities and digests; projection identity binds exact frontier, rule and selected relation/boundary/residual identities. New events create new frontiers; old projections never silently advance. Latest-only summaries do not prove completeness. Competing corrections, unresolved scope, missing causal inputs or stale basis remain residuals or stops according to the selected projection law.

grounding.quote:
Every event carries its declared scope class. `event_for` is present only
when the scope law names one exact occurrence.

constraints.statement: Every event declares scope class. event_for is present only where scope law names one exact occurrence. Subject-wide, publication-wide and other occurrence-independent facts remain independent.

grounding.quote:
Every material operation and judgment
resolves an existing owner-issued grant. Copying a profile record or
adopting the profile transfers no authority (P6).

constraints.statement: The profile grants no semantic, operation, evaluation, admission, decision, correction, continuation or closure authority; every material operation/judgment resolves an existing owner-issued grant. Copying/adoption transfers none. Only Product authority adopts, under referenced PRODUCT_DEFINITION §7. Adoption declares at least exact profile basis; subject/binding interpretation; mappings from Product concepts to sorts and relation kinds; operation, actor, executor, admission, projection and decision authorities; event-scope/frontier laws; invalidation/re-entry conditions; and qualification evidence that no Product distinction was lost. Absent or incomplete adoption leaves the profile available but inactive for that Product.

conditions: Publication bytes exist.
constraints.statement: TraversalOccurrenceSignature has exactly kind='stdo.traversal-occurrence-signature', schema_version=1, exact calculus_basis_identity, absolute calculus_signature_schema_clause_ref, sorted nonempty occurrence_signature_clause_refs and profile_member_sha256. Identity is sha256(JCS(signature)) using RFC 8785.
